headline: Brookfield earnings flat as buyback pace accelerates
summary_short: Brookfield's Q1 FY2026 revenue was $18.58B (+3.5% y/y, -7.8% q/q) as net income attributable to shareholders rose to $102M (+39.7% y/y, EPS $0.03) on higher equity-accounted income and fair-value gains, while distributable earnings held roughly flat at $1.55B.
summary_long: Revenue of $18.58B rose 3.5% y/y (-7.8% q/q) on inflation-indexed growth in Infrastructure and Energy, partly offset by dispositions rolling off. Net income was $1.04B; $102M was attributable to shareholders (+39.7% y/y, EPS $0.03), with $940M to non-controlling interests. The y/y gain reflects an $820M rise in equity-accounted income (a U.S. semiconductor facility, U.S. office/retail revaluations) and $781M higher fair-value changes, partly offset by a $515M drop in disposition gains and $190M higher interest expense. Gross margin fell 114bps y/y to 23.9%. Distributable earnings were $1.55B, flat y/y: Asset Management DE +5% to $922M on 12% fee-bearing-capital growth; Wealth Solutions DE flat at $430M. Corporate liquidity was $5.5B; BN/BAM share repurchases exceeded $1B in the quarter.

drivers.explanation: Growth from inflation-indexed rate increases and organic growth in the Infrastructure and Energy segments, partly offset by the absence of contributions from net dispositions over the trailing twelve months.
Direct costs rose $688M (inflation and organic growth in Infrastructure/Energy), outpacing the $636M revenue increase, which mechanically compresses the consolidated gross margin.

An $820M increase in equity-accounted income (a U.S. semiconductor facility; U.S. office/retail revaluations) and $781M higher fair-value gains, partly offset by a $515M drop in disposition gains and $190M higher interest expense.
Mirrors the swing in net income attributable to shareholders on a roughly stable diluted share count (2,367M vs 2,383M a year ago).

Distributable earnings of $1.55B were roughly flat y/y as 5% growth in Asset Management DE (higher fee-bearing capital) offset flat Wealth Solutions DE; the company accelerated buybacks, repurchasing over $1B of BN and BAM shares in the quarter.

confidence_notes: Primary source is Exhibit 99.1 (Interim Report to Shareholders) to the Form 6-K; the cover 6-K document itself (a2026-q16xkcover.htm) is only a wrapper with no results narrative. reported_at uses the 6-K filing date (2026-05-15), which is more authoritative than the shard's quarter-end placeholder eventDate (2026-03-31) — flagging per the real-report-date rule; the shard's eventDate was not modified. Brookfield reports under IFRS as a foreign private issuer; net income attributable to shareholders ($102M) is a small fraction of consolidated net income ($1.04B) because most operating businesses are majority-owned by non-controlling interests/perpetual affiliates (BIP, BEP, BBUC) — this structurally depresses net margin and isn't a standalone profitability signal. Distributable earnings (DE) and fee-related earnings (FRE) are non-IFRS measures Brookfield itself uses as primary performance metrics; captured separately in extendedMetrics. EPS reflects the 3-for-2 stock split completed October 9, 2025 (prior-period figures restated).
